To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of nested annotation yields an improvement over the use of flat annotation; (2) the use of a simple method for modelling nesting yields an improvement over a more elaborate method; (3) the use of the most elaborate method yields the best results; (4) the best results are obtained by using a combination of the three methods
the best performance is achieved by the method that uses the most information about the context of a candidate nested entity, namely the surrounding words and the tags of the surrounding words.

(a) the use of a simple rule-based method is the most effective approach for recognising nested entities, (b) a more complex rule-based method, that takes into account the entity type, yields a similar performance to the simpler rule-based method, and (c) the use of machine learning to model the entity type does not yield a significant improvement over the simpler rule-based approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of nested entities in biomedical text and the development of a novel method that can be used for the recognition of nested named entities in general.
recognising and modelling NE structures, which can be useful for downstream applications that involve NEs.
developing techniques that can be applied to the problem of recognising nested entities.

the best results are achieved with the use of a simple and efficient technique for modelling the nested structure.
the use of the best method for recognising nested entities yields the best performance.

the method that is based on a simple rule-based approach performs best, followed by the method that is trained on flat annotation with a simple rule-based post-processing, and the method that is also trained on flat annotation but with a complex rule-based post-processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best performance is obtained when using a combination of the three methods, with the best results being obtained on a data set with nested NE annotation.
the best performing model is the one that uses a combination of two different approaches.
the use of a single tagger to recognise both nested and flat NEs can achieve comparable results with a dedicated nested tagger.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to train a sequence tagger on flat annotation and use it to recognise nested structures.
it is feasible to recognise nested NEs using a sequence-based approach.
it is possible to train a sequence tagger to recognise nested entities using flat training data, and that a simple method that is based on a single pass over the input text performs well.
